additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

patient_info.stressor_event: Foreclosure on a mortgage or loan
patient_info.stressor: After a period of stretched finances, last-minute travel spending, and rising housing costs in West Palm Beach, Cassidy and her spouse faced foreclosure proceedings that brought legal notices, bank calls, and tense conversations into the center of their home life. Over the next 1 year and 9 months, what began as anger and suspicion about the loan process became a set of fixed beliefs about the foreclosure and the people involved, persisting despite documents, counseling from a housing nonprofit, and her spouse’s attempts to review the timeline with her. The beliefs increasingly affected her interactions at work and in the community, especially when ordinary financial or administrative issues seemed to confirm her interpretation. She was connected with psychiatric care after a housing counselor, noticing that practical foreclosure planning sessions repeatedly became dominated by the same unchangeable explanations, recommended an evaluation and helped her schedule the appointment.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house, and no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My marriage has gotten more tense because foreclosure conversations keep turning into arguments, and at work I have had a few tense exchanges with managers over ordinary paperwork. I am still working, but people are more careful around me now.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 1 year and 9 months, since the foreclosure notices and bank calls started taking over our home life.
